{{Short description|Stability notion for nonlinear control systems with external inputs}}
'''Input-to-state stability (ISS)'''<ref name=MCT>Eduardo D. Sontag. Mathematical Control Theory: Finite-Dimensional Systems. Springer-Verlag, London, 1998</ref><ref name=Khalil>Hassan K. Khalil.  Nonlinear Systems.  Prentice Hall, 2002.</ref><ref name=KaJ11 /><ref name=Son08 /><ref name=SIREVMironPrieu /><ref name="Mir23">{{cite book | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-14674-9 | doi=10.1007/978-3-031-14674-9 | title=Input-to-State Stability | series=Communications and Control Engineering | date=2023 | isbn=978-3-031-14673-2 }}</ref> is a stability notion widely used to study stability of nonlinear [[Control theory|control systems]] with external inputs. Roughly speaking, a control system is ISS if it is globally asymptotically stable in the absence of external inputs and if its trajectories are bounded by a function of the size of the input for all sufficiently large times.
The importance of ISS is due to the fact that the concept has bridged the gap between [[Input-Output stability|input–output]] and [[Lyapunov stability|state-space methods]], widely used within the control systems community.

ISS unified the Lyapunov and input-output stability theories and revolutionized our view on stabilization of nonlinear systems, design of robust nonlinear [[state observer|observers]], stability of nonlinear interconnected control systems, nonlinear [[Observability|detectability]] theory, and supervisory [[adaptive control]]. 
This made ISS the dominating stability paradigm in [[nonlinear control]] theory, with such diverse applications as robotics, [[mechatronics]], [[systems biology]], electrical and [[aerospace engineering]], to name a few.

The notion of ISS was introduced for systems described by ordinary differential equations by [[Eduardo Sontag]] in 1989.<ref name=Coprime1989>Eduardo D. Sontag. Smooth stabilization implies coprime factorization. IEEE Trans. Autom. Control, 34(4):435–443, 1989.</ref>

Since that the concept was successfully used for many other classes of control systems including systems governed by partial differential equations, retarded systems, hybrid systems, etc.<ref name=SIREVMironPrieu>[https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/19M1291248 A. Mironchenko, Ch. Prieur. Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems: recent results and open questions]. SIAM Review, 62(3):529–614, 2020.</ref>

== Definition ==

Consider a [[time-invariant system]] of [[ordinary differential equation]]s of the form

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\dot{x} = f(x,u), \ x(t) \in \mathbb{R}^n, 
</math>|{{EquationRef|1}}}}

where <math>u:\mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}^m</math> is a [[Lebesgue measure|Lebesgue measurable]] [[Essential supremum and essential infimum|essentially bounded]] external input and <math>f</math> is a [[Lipschitz continuity|Lipschitz continuous]] function w.r.t. the first argument uniformly w.r.t. the second one. This ensures that there exists a unique [[absolute continuity|absolutely continuous]] solution of the system ({{EquationNote|1}}).

To define ISS and related properties, we exploit the following classes of [[comparison function]]s. We denote by <math>\mathcal{K}</math> the set of continuous increasing functions <math> \gamma:\R_+ \to \R_+ </math>  with  <math> \gamma(0)=0 </math> and <math>\mathcal{L}</math> the set of continuous strictly decreasing functions <math> \gamma:\R_+ \to \R_+ </math>  with  <math> \lim_{r\to\infty} \gamma(r) = 0 </math>. Then we can denote <math> \beta \in \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} </math> as functions where <math> \beta(\cdot,t) \in \mathcal{K} </math> for all <math> t \geq 0 </math> and <math> \beta(r,\cdot) \in \mathcal{L} </math> for all <math> r > 0 </math>.

System ({{EquationNote|1}}) is called '''globally asymptotically stable at zero (0-GAS)''' if the corresponding system with zero input
{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\dot{x} = f(x,0), \ x(t) \in \mathbb{R}^n, 
</math>|{{EquationRef|WithoutInputs}}}}
is globally [[Lyapunov stability|asymptotically stable]], that is there exist 
<math> \beta \in \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} </math> so that for all initial values 
<math> x_0 </math> and all times <math> t \geq 0 </math> the following estimate is valid for solutions of ({{EquationNote|WithoutInputs}})
{{NumBlk|:|<math>
|x(t)| \leq \beta(|x_0|,t). 
</math>|{{EquationRef|GAS-Estimate}}}}

System ({{EquationNote|1}}) is called '''input-to-state stable (ISS)''' if there exist functions 
<math> \gamma \in \mathcal{K} </math> and  <math> \beta \in \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} </math> so that for all initial values <math> x_0 </math>, all admissible inputs <math> u </math> and all times <math> t \geq 0 </math> the following inequality holds
{{NumBlk|:|<math>
|x(t)| \leq \beta(|x_0|,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\infty}). 
</math>|{{EquationRef|2}}}}

The function  <math>\gamma</math> in the above inequality is called the '''gain'''.

Clearly, an ISS system is 0-GAS as well as [[BIBO stability|BIBO stable]] (if we put the output equal to the state of the system). The converse implication is in general not true.

It can be also proved that if <math>\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} |u(t)| = 0</math>, then <math>\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty} |x(t)| = 0 </math>.

== Characterizations of input-to-state stability property ==

For an understanding of ISS its restatements in terms of other stability properties are of great importance.

System ({{EquationNote|1}}) is called '''globally stable (GS)''' if there exist  
<math> \gamma, \sigma \in \mathcal{K} </math> such that <math>\forall x_0 </math>, <math>\forall u</math> and <math>\forall t \geq 0 </math> it holds that

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
|x(t)| \leq \sigma(|x_0|) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\infty}). 
</math>|{{EquationRef|GS}}}}

System ({{EquationNote|1}}) satisfies the '''asymptotic gain (AG) property''' if there exists  
<math>\gamma \in \mathcal{K} </math>: <math>\forall x_0 </math>, <math>\forall u</math> it holds that

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\limsup_{t \to \infty}|x(t)| \leq \gamma(\|u\|_{\infty}). 
</math>|{{EquationRef|AG}}}}

The following statements are equivalent for sufficiently regular right-hand side <math>f</math><ref name=NewCharacterisations>Eduardo D. Sontag and [[Yuan Wang (control theorist)|Yuan Wang]]. [https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20110401123458/http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~sontag/PUBDIR/FTP_DIR/new-iss.pdf New characterizations of input-to-state stability]. IEEE Trans. Autom. Control, 41(9):1283–1294, 1996.</ref>

1. ({{EquationNote|1}}) is ISS

2. ({{EquationNote|1}}) is GS and has the AG property

3. ({{EquationNote|1}}) is 0-GAS and has the AG property

The proof of this result as well as many other characterizations of ISS can be found in the papers
<ref name=NewCharacterisations /> and.<ref name=Characterisations /> 
Other characterizations of ISS that are valid under very mild restrictions on the regularity of the rhs <math>f</math> and are applicable to more general infinite-dimensional systems, have been shown in.<ref name=MiW18b>Andrii Mironchenko and Fabian Wirth. Characterizations of input-to-state stability for infinite-dimensional systems. IEEE Trans. Autom. Control, 63(6): 1602-1617, 2018.</ref>

== ISS-Lyapunov functions ==

:

An important tool for the verification of ISS are [[ISS-Lyapunov function]]s.

A smooth function <math>V: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}_+</math> is called an ISS-Lyapunov function for ({{EquationNote|1}}), if <math>\exists \psi_1,\psi_2 \in \mathcal{K}_{\infty} </math> and <math>\alpha,\chi \in  \mathcal{K} </math>, such that:
::<math> 
\psi_1(|x|) \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(|x|), \quad \forall x \in  \mathbb{R}^n 
</math> 
and 
<math>\forall x \in \mathbb{R}^n, \; \forall u\in \mathbb{R}^m</math> it holds:
:: <math> 
 |x| \geq \chi(|u|) \  \Rightarrow  \  \nabla V \cdot f(x,u) \leq -\alpha(|x|),
</math>

The function <math>\chi</math> is called '''Lyapunov gain'''.

If a system ({{EquationNote|1}}) is without inputs (i.e. <math>u \equiv 0</math>), then the last implication reduces to the condition

::<math> 
\nabla V \cdot f(x,u) \leq -\alpha(|x|),\ \forall x \neq 0,
</math>

which tells us that  <math> V </math> is a "classic" [[Lyapunov function]].

An important result due to E. Sontag and Y. Wang is that a system ({{EquationNote|1}}) is ISS [[if and only if]] there exists a smooth ISS-Lyapunov function for it.<ref name=Characterisations>Eduardo D. Sontag and [[Yuan Wang (control theorist)|Yuan Wang]]. [http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~sontag/PUBDIR/FTP_DIR/converse-iss.pdf On characterizations of the input-to-state stability property] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703102042/http://math.rutgers.edu/~sontag/PUBDIR/FTP_DIR/converse-iss.pdf |date=2013-07-03 }}. Systems Control Lett., 24(5):351–359, 1995.</ref>

== Examples ==

Consider a system
::<math> 
\dot{x}=-x^3+ux^2.
</math>

Define a candidate ISS-Lyapunov function <math>V:\R \to \R_+ </math> by
<math> 
V(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^2, \quad \forall x \in \R.
</math>

<math> 
\dot{V}(x)=\nabla V \cdot (-x^3+ux^2) = -x^4 + ux^3.
</math>

Choose a Lyapunov gain <math> \chi</math> by 
::<math> \chi(r):= \frac{1}{1-\epsilon}r </math>.

Then we obtain that for <math> x,u:\ |x| \geq \chi(|u|)</math>  it holds

::<math> 
\dot{V}(x) \leq  -|x|^4 + (1-\epsilon)|x|^4 = -\epsilon|x|^4.
</math>

This shows that  <math> V </math> is an ISS-Lyapunov function for a considered system with the Lyapunov gain  <math> \chi</math>.

== Interconnections of ISS systems ==

One of the main features of the ISS framework is the possibility to study stability properties of interconnections of input-to-state stable systems.

Consider the system given by

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\left\{ 
\begin{array}{l}
\dot{x}_{i}=f_{i}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n},u),\\
i=1,\ldots,n.
\end{array}
\right.
</math>|{{EquationRef|WholeSys}}}}

Here <math>u \in L_{\infty}(\R_+,\R^m)</math>, <math>x_{i}(t)\in \R^{p_i}</math> and <math>f_i</math> are Lipschitz continuous in <math>x_i</math> uniformly with respect to the inputs from the <math>i</math>-th subsystem.

For the <math>i</math>-th subsystem of ({{EquationNote|WholeSys}}) the definition of an ISS-Lyapunov function can be written as follows.

A smooth function <math>V_{i}:\R^{p_{i}} \to \R_{+}</math> is an ISS-Lyapunov function (ISS-LF)
for the <math>i</math>-th subsystem of ({{EquationNote|WholeSys}}), if there exist
functions <math>\psi_{i1},\psi_{i2}\in\mathcal{K}_{\infty}</math>, <math>\chi_{ij},\chi_{i}\in  \mathcal{K}</math>,
<math>j=1,\ldots,n</math>, <math>j \neq i</math>, <math>\chi_{ii}:=0</math> and a positive-definite function <math>\alpha_{i}</math>, such that:

::<math>
\psi_{i1}(|x_{i}|)\leq V_{i}(x_{i})\leq\psi_{i2}(|x_{i}|),\quad \forall x_{i}\in \R^{p_{i}}
</math> 
and <math> \forall x_{i}\in \R^{p_{i}},\; \forall u\in \R^m</math> it holds

::<math> 
V_i(x_{i})\geq\max\{ \max_{j=1}^{n}\chi_{ij}(V_{j}(x_{j})),\chi_{i}(|u|)\} \ \Rightarrow\ \nabla V_i (x_i) \cdot f_{i}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n},u) \leq-\alpha_{i}(V_{i}(x_{i})).
</math>

=== Cascade interconnections ===

Cascade interconnections are a special type of interconnection, where the dynamics of the <math>i</math>-th subsystem does not depend on the states of the subsystems <math>1,\ldots,i-1</math>. Formally, the cascade interconnection can be written as

::<math>
\left\{ 
\begin{array}{l}
\dot{x}_{i}=f_{i}(x_{i},\ldots,x_{n},u),\\
i=1,\ldots,n.
\end{array}
\right.
</math>

If all subsystems of the above system are ISS, then the whole cascade interconnection is also ISS.<ref name=Coprime1989 /><ref name=Son08>Eduardo D. Sontag. Input to state stability: basic concepts and results. In Nonlinear and optimal control theory, volume 1932 of Lecture Notes in Math., pages 163–220, Berlin, 2008. Springer</ref>

In contrast to cascades of ISS systems, the cascade interconnection of 0-GAS systems is in general not 0-GAS. The following example illustrates this fact. Consider a system given by

{{NumBlk|:|<math> 
\left\{ 
\begin{array}{l}
\dot{x}=-x + yx^2, \\
\dot{y}=-y.
\end{array}
\right.
</math>|{{EquationRef|Ex_GAS}}}}

Both subsystems of this system are 0-GAS, but for sufficiently large initial states <math>(x_0,y_0)</math> and for a certain finite time <math>t^*</math> it holds <math>x(t) \to \infty</math> for  <math>t \to t^*</math>, i.e. the system ({{EquationNote|Ex_GAS}}) exhibits [[finite escape time]], and thus is not 0-GAS.

=== Feedback interconnections ===

The interconnection structure of subsystems is characterized by the internal Lyapunov gains <math>\chi_{ij}</math>. The question, whether the interconnection ({{EquationNote|WholeSys}}) is ISS, depends on the properties of the '''gain operator''' <math>\Gamma:\R_{+}^{n}\rightarrow\R_{+}^{n}</math> defined by 
::<math>
\Gamma(s):=\left(\max_{j=1}^{n}\chi_{1j}(s_{j}),\ldots,\max_{j=1}^{n}\chi_{nj}(s_{j})\right),\ s\in\R_{+}^{n}.
</math>

The following '''small-gain theorem''' establishes a sufficient condition for ISS of the interconnection of ISS systems. Let <math>V_{i}</math> be an ISS-Lyapunov function for <math>i</math>-th subsystem of ({{EquationNote|WholeSys}}) with corresponding gains <math>\chi_{ij}</math>, <math>i=1,\ldots,n</math>. If the nonlinear '''small-gain condition'''
{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\Gamma(s)\not\geq s,\ \forall\ s\in\R_{+}^{n}\backslash\left\{ 0\right\}
</math>|{{EquationRef|SGC}}}}
holds, then the whole interconnection is ISS.<ref>Zhong-Ping Jiang, Iven M. Y. Mareels, and [[Yuan Wang (control theorist)|Yuan Wang]]. A Lyapunov formulation of the nonlinear small-gain theorem for interconnected ISS systems. Automatica J. IFAC, 32(8):1211–1215, 1996.</ref><ref>Sergey Dashkovskiy, Björn S. Rüffer, and Fabian R. Wirth. An ISS Lyapunov function for networks of ISS systems. In Proceedings of the 17th International Symposium on Mathematical Theory of Networks and Systems (MTNS), Kyoto, Japan, July 24–28, 2006, pages 77–82, 2006</ref>

Small-gain condition  ({{EquationNote|SGC}}) holds iff for each cycle in <math>\Gamma</math> (that is for all <math>(k_1,...,k_p) \in \{1,...,n\}^p</math>, where <math>k_1=k_p</math>) and for all <math>s>0</math> it holds
::<math>
\gamma_{k_1k_2} \circ \gamma_{k_2k_3} \circ \ldots \circ \gamma_{k_{p-1}k_p} (s) < s.
</math>
The small-gain condition in this form is called also cyclic small-gain condition.

== Related stability concepts ==

=== Integral ISS (iISS) ===
System ({{EquationNote|1}}) is called integral input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist functions <math> \alpha, \gamma \in \mathcal{K} </math> and  <math> \beta \in \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} </math> so that for all initial values <math> x_0 </math>, all admissible inputs <math> u </math> and all times <math> t \geq 0 </math> the following inequality holds

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\alpha(|x(t)|) \leq \beta(|x_0|,t) + \int_0^t \gamma(|u(s)|)ds. 
</math>|{{EquationRef|3}}}}

In contrast to ISS systems, if a system is integral ISS, its trajectories may be unbounded even for bounded inputs. To see this put <math> \alpha(r)=\gamma(r)=r </math> for all <math> r \geq 0 </math> and take <math>u \equiv c= const</math>. Then the estimate ({{EquationNote|3}}) takes the form
::<math>
|x(t)| \leq \beta(|x_0|,t) + \int_0^t cds = \beta(|x_0|,t) + ct,
</math>
and the right hand side grows to infinity as  <math> t \to \infty </math>.

As in the ISS framework, Lyapunov methods play a central role in iISS theory.

A smooth function <math>V: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}_+</math> is called an iISS-Lyapunov function for ({{EquationNote|1}}), if <math>\exists \psi_1,\psi_2 \in \mathcal{K}_{\infty} </math>, <math>\chi \in  \mathcal{K} </math> and [[positive-definite function]]  <math>\alpha</math>, such that:

::<math> 
\psi_1(|x|) \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(|x|), \quad \forall x \in  \mathbb{R}^n 
</math> 
and 
<math>\forall x \in \mathbb{R}^n, \; \forall u\in \mathbb{R}^m</math> it holds:
:: <math> 
\dot{V} = \nabla V \cdot f(x,u) \leq -\alpha(|x|) + \gamma(|u|).
</math>

An important result due to D. Angeli, E. Sontag and Y. Wang is that system ({{EquationNote|1}}) is integral ISS if and only if there exists an iISS-Lyapunov function for it.

Note that in the formula above <math>\alpha</math> is assumed to be only [[positive-definite function|positive definite]]. 
It can be easily proved,<ref>See Remark  2.4. in Eduardo D. Sontag and [[Yuan Wang (control theorist)|Yuan Wang]]. On characterizations of the input-to-state stability property. Systems Control Lett., 24(5):351–359, 1995</ref> that if <math>V</math> is an iISS-Lyapunov function with <math>\alpha \in \mathcal{K}_{\infty}</math>, then <math>V</math> is actually an ISS-Lyapunov function for a system ({{EquationNote|1}}).

This shows in particular, that every ISS system is integral ISS. The converse implication is not true, as the following example shows. Consider the system

::<math>
\dot{x}=-\arctan{x} + u.
</math>

This system is not ISS, since for large enough inputs the trajectories are unbounded. However, it is integral ISS with an iISS-Lyapunov function <math>V</math> defined by 
::<math>
V(x)=x \arctan{x}.
</math>

=== Local ISS (LISS) ===
An important role are also played by local versions of the ISS property. A system ({{EquationNote|1}}) is called '''locally ISS (LISS)''' if there exist a constant <math>\rho>0</math> and functions

<math> \gamma \in \mathcal{K} </math> and  <math> \beta \in \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} </math> so that for all <math> x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n: \; |x_0| \leq \rho </math>, all admissible inputs <math> u: \|u\|_{\infty} \leq \rho </math> and all times <math> t \geq 0 </math> it holds that

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
|x(t)| \leq \beta(|x_0|,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\infty}). 
</math>|{{EquationRef|4}}}}

An interesting observation is that 0-GAS implies LISS.<ref>Lemma I.1, p.1285 in Eduardo D. Sontag and [[Yuan Wang (control theorist)|Yuan Wang]]. New characterizations of input-to-state stability. IEEE Trans. Autom. Control, 41(9):1283–1294, 1996</ref>

=== Other stability notions ===

Many other related to ISS stability notions have been introduced: incremental ISS, [[input-to-state dynamical stability]] (ISDS),<ref>Lars Grüne. Input-to-state dynamical stability and its Lyapunov function characterization. IEEE Trans. Autom. Control, 47(9):1499–1504, 2002.</ref> [[input-to-state practical stability]] (ISpS), [[input-to-output stability]] (IOS)<ref>Z.-P. Jiang, A. R. Teel, and L. Praly. Small-gain theorem for ISS systems and applications. Math. Control Signals Systems, 7(2):95–120, 1994.</ref> etc.

== ISS of time-delay systems ==

Consider the time-invariant [[Delay differential equation|time-delay system]]

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\dot{x}(t)=f(x^t,u(t)), \quad t > 0. 
</math>|{{EquationRef|TDS}}}}

Here <math>x^t\in C([-\theta,0];\R^N)</math> is the state of the system ({{EquationNote|TDS}}) at time <math>t</math>, <math>x^t(\tau)=x(t+\tau),\ \tau\in[-\theta,0]</math> and <math>f:C([-\theta,0];\R^N) \times \R^m</math> satisfies certain assumptions to guarantee existence and uniqueness of solutions of the system ({{EquationNote|TDS}}).

System ({{EquationNote|TDS}}) is ISS if and only if there exist functions <math>\beta\in \mathcal{KL}</math> and <math>\gamma\in\mathcal{K}</math> such that for every <math>\xi\in C(\left[-\theta,0\right],\R^N)</math>, every admissible input <math>u</math> and for all <math>t\in\R_+</math>, it holds that

{{NumBlk|:|<math>
\left|x(t)\right|\leq \beta(\left\|\xi\right\|_{\left[-\theta,0\right]},t) + \gamma(\left\|u\right\|_{\infty}).
</math>|{{EquationRef|ISS-TDS}}}}

In the ISS theory for time-delay systems two different Lyapunov-type sufficient conditions have been proposed: via ISS Lyapunov-Razumikhin functions<ref>Andrew R. Teel. Connections between Razumikhin-type theorems and the ISS nonlinear small gain theorem. IEEE Trans. Autom. Control, 43(7):960–964, 1998.</ref> and by ISS Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals.<ref>P. Pepe and Z.-P. Jiang. A Lyapunov-Krasovskii methodology for ISS and iISS of time-delay systems. Systems Control Lett., 55(12):1006–1014, 2006.</ref> For converse Lyapunov theorems for time-delay systems see.<ref>Iasson Karafyllis. Lyapunov theorems for systems described by retarded functional differential equations. Nonlinear Analysis: Theory, Methods & Applications, 64(3):590 – 617, 2006.</ref>

== ISS of other classes of systems ==

Input-to-state stability of the systems based on time-invariant ordinary differential equations is a quite developed theory, see a recent monograph.<ref name=Mir23/> However, ISS theory of other classes of systems is also being investigated for [[Time-variant system|time-variant ODE systems]]<ref>Yuandan Lin, [[Yuan Wang (control theorist)|Yuan Wang]], and Daizhan Cheng. On nonuniform and semi-uniform input-to-state stability for time-varying systems. In IFAC World Congress, Prague, 2005.</ref> and [[hybrid systems]].<ref>Chaohong Cai and Andrew R. Teel. Characterizations of input-to-state stability for hybrid systems. Systems & Control Letters, 58(1):47–53, 2009.</ref><ref>D. Nesic and A.R. Teel. A Lyapunov-based small-gain theorem for hybrid ISS systems. In Proceedings of the 47th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, Cancun, Mexico, Dec. 9-11, 2008, pages 3380–3385, 2008.</ref> In the last time also certain generalizations of ISS concepts to infinite-dimensional systems have been proposed.<ref>[http://www.ims.cuhk.edu.hk/~cis/2008.4/cis_8_4_04.pdf Bayu Jayawardhana, Hartmut Logemann, and Eugene P. Ryan. Infinite-dimensional feedback systems: the circle criterion and input-to-state stability]. Commun. Inf. Syst., 8(4):413–414, 2008.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00498-012-0090-2 | doi=10.1007/s00498-012-0090-2 | title=Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional control systems | date=2013 | last1=Dashkovskiy | first1=Sergey | last2=Mironchenko | first2=Andrii | journal=Mathematics of Control, Signals, and Systems | volume=25 | pages=1–35 | arxiv=1202.3325 }}</ref><ref name=KaJ11>Iasson Karafyllis and Zhong-Ping Jiang. Stability and stabilization of nonlinear systems. Communications and Control Engineering Series. Springer-Verlag London Ltd., London, 2011.</ref><ref>F. Mazenc and C. Prieur. Strict Lyapunov functions for semilinear parabolic partial differential equations. Mathematical Control and Related Fields, 1:231–250, June 2011.</ref>
